body_text: HF Foods Group to Acquire Searay Foods, a Highly Attractive Canadian Importer and Distributor of Ethnic and Specialty Seafood Products, Marking the Company's First International Expansion July 23, 2026 PDF Version Strategic entry into Canada through the Vancouver metro market, one of North America's premier specialty Asian foods markets with deep multicultural ties Reinforces HF Foods' positioning as the acquiror of choice, extending its proven M&A playbook into new geographies Transaction valued at approximately 5.0x Searay's 2025P Adjusted EBITDA and is expected to be immediately accretive to Margins and EPS Consideration to be funded through a combination of cash and HF Foods common stock HF Foods' reaffirms previously communicated target of expanding consolidated Adjusted EBITDA margin to 4.5%-5.0%+ over the next three to five years LAS VEGAS, July 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- HF Foods Group Inc. (NASDAQ: HFFG) (“HF Foods” or the “Company”), a leading distributor of international foodservice solutions to Asian restaurants and other businesses across the United States, today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Searay Foods Inc. and its related entities (“Searay”), a leading Canadian importer and distributor of ethnic and specialty frozen seafood, headquartered in Richmond, British Columbia. The transaction represents HF Foods’ first expansion outside the United States and is expected to close in Q3 2026, subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals. Under the terms of the agreement, HF Foods will acquire up to 100% of the outstanding equity interests of Searay for total consideration of approximately CAD$47.9 million (approximately US$35 million), representing approximately 5.0x Searay's 2025 Adjusted EBITDA of approximately CAD$9.6 million. Consideration will be funded through a combination of cash on hand and shares of HF Foods common stock, with final terms to be disclosed upon closing. Management Commentary “The acquisition of Searay is a pivotal milestone in HF Foods’ growth journey and the first step in our long-stated strategy to expand our platform beyond the United States,” said Felix Lin, President and Chief Executive Officer of HF Foods. “Searay has built an exceptional reputation over 25 years as a leading Canadian distributor of ethnic frozen seafood, with deep supplier relationships, a trusted multi-brand portfolio, and industry-leading margins. This transaction is consistent with the disciplined, accretive M&A strategy we have communicated to investors, and we are excited to combine Searay’s expertise in frozen seafood with HF Foods’ national distribution infrastructure to unlock meaningful cross-selling and supply chain synergies across both businesses.” “We are proud of what we have built at Searay over the past 25 years, and we believe HF Foods is the right partner to carry that legacy forward,” said Jack and Philip Chan, Co-Presidents and founders of Searay. “HF Foods’ scale, distribution network, and shared commitment to quality and customer service make this a natural combination. We look forward to working alongside the HF Foods team to accelerate Searay’s growth, including our ongoing expansion into the U.S. market.” Strategic Rationale First International Expansion: The transaction marks HF Foods’ entry into Canada and establishes a platform to pursue further growth across North America, consistent with the Company’s previously disclosed proven M&A playbook of geographic expansion, increased distribution capabilities, and new product categories. Complementary Product Portfolio: Searay’s ethnic frozen seafood offering, including its Searay Foods, Thai Best, Pinoy’s Best, Smart Fish, Diamond Shrimp, and Gold Label brands, broadens HF Foods’ specialty product assortment and deepens its presence in the seafood category, which represents approximately 36% of HF Foods’ existing net revenue. Cross-Border Synergies: Searay’s recently established U.S. operations, including its planned Los Angeles direct import operations, are expected to benefit from HF Foods’ existing distribution network, sourcing scale, and West Coast infrastructure. Attractive Financial Profile: Searay has demonstrated a revenue compound annual growth rate of approximately 15% from FY2019 to FY2024 and strong Normalized EBITDA margins of approximately 14-15%, supported by disciplined inventory management and long-tenured supplier and customer relationships. Accretive Transaction: The acquisition is expected to be accretive to HF Foods’ Adjusted EBITDA and margins, consistent with the Company’s previously communicated target of expanding consolidated Adjusted EBITDA margin to 4.5%-5.0%+ over the next three to five years. Transaction Details HF Foods will acquire up to 100% of Searay Foods Inc., Morgan Foods Inc., and Searay Foods USA Inc. for total consideration of approximately CAD$47.9 million (approximately US$35 million based on current exchange rates), representing approximately 5.0x Searay's 2025 Adjusted EBITDA of approximately CAD$9.6 million. The consideration is expected to be funded through a combination of cash on hand and newly issued shares of HF Foods common stock; the final split between cash and stock consideration will be disclosed at closing. Following the closing of the transaction, Searay's existing management team, led by incoming Chief Executive Officer Derick Ngan, is expected to continue to lead Searay's day-to-day operations as a subsidiary of HF Foods. The transaction is expected to close in Q3 2026, subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals. About HF Foods Group Inc. HF Foods Group Inc. is a leading marketer and distributor of fresh produce, frozen and dry food, and non-food products to primarily Asian restaurants and other foodservice customers throughout the United States. HF Foods aims to supply the increasing demand for Asian American restaurant cuisine, leveraging its nationwide network of distribution centers and its strong relations with growers and suppliers of fresh, high-quality specialty restaurant food products and supplies in the US and Asia. Headquartered in Las Vegas, Nevada, HF Foods trades on Nasdaq under the symbol “HFFG”. For more information, please visit www.hffoodsgroup.com. About Searay Foods Inc. Founded in 2000 and headquartered in Richmond, British Columbia, Searay Foods Inc. is a leading Canadian importer and distributor of branded ethnic and specialty frozen seafood, serving retail, wholesale, and restaurant customers across North America. Searay sources premium frozen seafood from more than 80 suppliers worldwide and distributes its products through six proprietary brands, including Searay Foods, Thai Best, Pinoy’s Best, Smart Fish, Diamond Shrimp, and Gold Label. title: The Best of Both Worlds: Your Dream Retirement, Without the Challenges of Coastal Living
body_text: The Best of Both Worlds: Your Dream Retirement, Without the Challenges of Coastal Living Tri Pointe Homes • July 8, 2026 Share this article Many people dream of a retirement that includes sandy beaches, salty air, and an overall slower pace of life. The idea of beach life is undeniably appealing, but is true coastal living everything you imagine it will be? Retirement is more than just where you live; it’s about how you spend your time. It’s about being close to the people you love, exploring the places you’ve always wanted to visit, and slowing down to enjoy life and its every moment. Altis at Serenity™ by Tri Pointe Homes® offers the retirement lifestyle you imagined without some of the often-overlooked challenges of coastal living. You get the comfort and convenience of Raleigh-area living with the luxuries of the beach still just a short drive away. Altis at Serenity is a resort-style 55+ active adult community in Fuquay-Varina that offers residents the best of both worlds and a chance to discover their New Next. Stay Connected to Family, Travel, and Adventure Retirement should expand your world, not shrink it. Staying in a central location puts you in the middle of everywhere, perfect for spontaneous weekend adventures and making travel plans even easier. Located in the heart of North Carolina, Fuquay-Varina offers retirees easy access to any part of the state, whether that’s the grandkids’ house, the mountains, or the beach. Fuquay-Varina is a short two-hour drive from prime North Carolina shores like Wrightsville Beach and Carolina Beach, and a three-hour drive to the breathtaking North Carolina mountains. It is also just a 30-minute drive to the Raleigh–Durham International Airport (RDU) for any other national or international travel plans. Let every sunrise of your retirement contain infinite possibilities. Imagine waking up one morning with a car packed and ready for a quick drive down to the beach, and the next setting off to enjoy the mountains. By the end of the week, you could be boarding a direct flight from RDU to your next adventure abroad. Explore New Interests Without the Tourist Crowds The Triangle is a thriving area that offers endless chances to stay active and engaged. From museums to fine dining, there is always something new to experience. As home to major universities such as North Carolina State University, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, and Duke University, the Triangle provides opportunities for lifelong learning. North Carolina residents age 65 and older are eligible to audit courses through NC State’s Senior Auditors Program , making it easy to continue exploring new interests and expand your mind in retirement. Unlike many coastal communities that experience surges of seasonal visitors, the Triangle offers these amenities year-round without the traffic, crowds, and lines that come with tourism. This way, you can enjoy a fulfilling lifestyle while maintaining a sense of comfort and community that makes retirement truly relaxing. While living on the beach sounds appealing, full-time coastal living can come with added maintenance , increased exposure to severe weather, and higher insurance costs . In recent years, homeowners along North Carolina’s coastline have seen insurance premiums rise, with some coastal properties experiencing increases between 50% and 99% from 2019 to 2024, according to Forbes. Salty air and humidity can take a toll on homes and vehicles over time, adding unnecessary emotional and financial stress to your retirement. Retiring in Fuquay-Varina means enjoying a welcoming community with easy access to the excitement and opportunities of the surrounding Triangle area. Closer to home, residents can enjoy Fuquay-Varina’s charming downtown district , locally owned shops and restaurants, and community events. This creates the perfect balance of convenience, relaxation, and adventure, all while maintaining that peaceful small-town charm. In fact, Fuquay-Varina has consistently been ranked among the top small towns in America by experts at Homes.com and WalletHub . It has also been ranked as one of the best places for remote workers - perfect for those active adults still going strong in their careers or those recent retirees finally chasing an entrepreneurial dream. Why Retirement at Altis at Serenity Is the Best Choice for Your Next Chapter Retirement isn’t about choosing between adventure and comfort; it’s about creating a lifestyle that can give you both. At Altis at Serenity in Fuquay-Varina, residents can create a lifestyle built around what matters most to them. Enjoy amenities like the pool, yoga studio, and fitness center while building connections with other adults your age. Fuquay-Varina offers its own unique charm and welcoming atmosphere and being just south of the Triangle, Altis at Serenity offers the chance to create a retirement lifestyle centered around relaxation, connection, and new experiences. Start your next chapter in a community designed for the retirement you have always imagined at Altis at Serenity . ALL MATERIALS HAVE BEEN PREPARED FOR GENERAL INFORMATION PURPOSES ONLY. title: Ford's Quality Momentum Continues: JD Power 2026 APEAL Study Shows Sustained Improvement
body_text: If you've been following our journey at Ford, you know we’ve been incredibly focused on fundamentally transforming our quality. Recently, we earned the number one spot among mainstream brands in the JD Power 2026 Initial Quality Study (IQS).SM That was a tremendous milestone for us, proving that our engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing processes are reducing defects. But building a great vehicle isn't just about what doesn't go wrong. It’s also about what goes incredibly right. That’s why I am proud to share the results of the JD Power 2026 U.S. APEAL Study,SM which demonstrate that we are making sustained strides in improving the things people genuinely love about their Ford vehicles. If you aren't familiar with the APEAL (Automotive Performance, Execution, and Layout) Study, it measures a customer's emotional attachment and level of excitement with their new vehicle's design, performance, safety, usability, and comfort after the first 90 days. It asks the question: after the "new car" feeling has worn off and real-life sets in, do you still love what you drive? For Ford owners, the results are telling. The Ford brand improved 11 points overall to an 849 index score, jumping from 12th to 9th among mainstream brands and positioning us well above the mainstream average. I’m proud of the consistency we are seeing in our passion products. Two of the nameplates that carried Ford to the APEAL podium last year did it again this year: the Ford Mustang was named the most appealing Sporty Car for the second year running, and the Ford Super Duty was named the most appealing Large Heavy-Duty Pickup for the third consecutive year. Ford earned four top-three finishes out of 10 award eligible series, including the two segment awards. When you put our IQS and APEAL results together, they tell a single, powerful story: This kind of consistency doesn’t happen by accident. We also earned best-in-segment IQS awards for the second straight year for the F-150, Mustang, and Super Duty, with seven of our ten models placing in the top three of their respective segments — the highest percentage of any automaker. Overall, we are continuing to provide a better experience for our customers by reducing quality issues with new vehicles and simultaneously improving the features our products provide. As we move forward, quality and customer experience are no longer siloed at Ford. They are a shared, uncompromising discipline running through our design studios, our engineering teams, our manufacturing plants, and our suppliers. We are building checks and balances that are built to last, and these latest results show that our focus on what you actually experience behind the wheel is paying off. We still have work to do, but we are absolutely on the right track. Thank you for continuing on this journey with us. Josh Halliburton is executive director of quality at Ford Motor Company.

title: Introducing new products and model updates to help you build, deploy, and scale Voice AI applications
summary: Today, we’re introducing a powerful new suite of products and model updates to the AssemblyAI platform that help you build, deploy, and scale your Voice AI applications.
body_text: We have released new and improved models since this article was published. See our docs for our most current model offerings. Today, we’re introducing a powerful new suite of products and model updates to the AssemblyAI platform that help you build, deploy, and scale your Voice AI applications: New products: Speech Understanding : Advanced capabilities from speaker identification to translation LLM Gateway : One API for your entire voice-to-intelligence pipeline Product Improvements: Universal enhancements : 99 languages, automatic code-switching, and improved speaker diarization with 64% fewer speaker counting errors Slam updates: Industry-leading accuracy improvements for critical terms and formatting Guardrails: Comprehensive protection to ensure only high-quality, safe, and compliant content flows through your applications. These updates eliminate the complexity between raw audio and production-ready Voice AI applications, allowing you to build powerful products and get them to market faster. The industry's best products are built on the industry's best models Voice AI has evolved over the last year from experimental features to critical infrastructure powering today’s top products. Voice agents are handling customer calls. Meeting intelligence is driving business decisions. Medical scribes are transforming doctors’ workflows. But most teams still spend their time stitching together basic functionality like language detection, speaker identification, and LLM integration, instead of shipping differentiated products. AssemblyAI’s platform delivers the highest-quality foundation so you can build exceptional Voice AI applications. Best-in-class speech-to-text accuracy meets powerful capabilities that transform raw speech into structured, intelligent data. Three new products for production Voice AI 1. Speech Understanding: Beyond basic speech-to-text Convert speech into structured, ready-to-use data. These purpose-built, LLM-powered features turn transcripts into intelligence instantly, giving you intelligent outputs out of the box. Advanced Capabilities Advanced speaker identification: Label speakers by role or by name Custom formatting: Define domain-specific formatting for your industry Translation: Receive transcripts in your preferred language across 89 supported languages Built for teams who want smarter outputs rather than more data. No extra integrations, just immediate understanding. 2. Guardrails: Production-ready safety Guardrails give you comprehensive protection at every stage of your voice AI pipeline including validating inputs and filtering outputs. Guardrails ensure that only high-quality, safe, compliant content flows through your applications. Safety Guardrails Profanity filtering: Automatically detect and remove inappropriate language Content moderation: Block sensitive or harmful content before it reaches downstream systems PII redaction: Remove personal information from text and audio outputs, available in 50+ languages Operational Guardrails Speech Threshold: Transcribe only files with a minimum percentage of spoken audio. Set start and end of transcript: Limit transcription to sections containing speech. With Guardrails, you can ensure that you’re stopping unsafe content immediately, and keep it from impacting your application or end users. 3. LLM Gateway: From audio to insights in one platform With LLM Gateway, you can consolidate your Voice AI application stack across speech-to-text, speech understanding, and LLM insights into one platform. LLM gateway lets you test and validate workflows, including summarization, sentiment analysis, redaction, and more, without juggling vendors or managing separate integrations. LLM Gateway gives you a unified Voice AI Platform LLM-compatible API for transcript-to-intelligence tasks like summarization, insight extraction, and more Route requests to leading LLMs including GPT, OpenAI, Gemini, and others directly from the AssemblyAI platform Integrated prompting on transcripts, allowing you to go straight from audio to insights without copying data between tools Unified billing and usage management across providers Many teams spend valuable engineering time maintaining complex post-processing pipelines to summarize calls, extract insights, or classify sentiment. LLM Gateway removes that complexity and lets developers focus on building great products for their customers. Enhanced foundation: Speech-to-text model improvements Universal-2: The proven foundation Universal-2 continues to set the standard for global, high-quality speech-to-text with significant improvements: Highlights 99 languages with automatic language detection Automatic code-switching between English and other languages 64% reduction in speaker counting errors for mid- to long-duration audio files (longer than 2 minutes) 200-word key term support Works across applications as a general-purpose speech-to-text model Starting at $0.15/hour The quality speaks for itself: Slam: When precision matters Our Slam (Speech Language AI Model), currently in beta, continues to evolve with industry-leading accuracy improvements for the most demanding use cases. Since the beta launch, we've enhanced speaker diarization, added multi-channel processing with improved timestamp prediction, and significantly reduced hallucinations. Highlights Up to 57% accuracy gains across alphanumerics, emails, addresses, financial statements, and organization names 1,000-word context-aware key term prompting to improve domain expertise up to 45% for precision-critical applications Built for human conversation analysis matching Universal's WER and speaker count accuracy while delivering superior formatting Starting at $0.27/hour API update: Intelligent model fallback To simplify model selection, we’re updating our API interface so customers can specify multiple models in priority order. Set Slam as your default for maximum precision, and the API will automatically fallback to Universal when you need broader language coverage. Real-world results AssemblyAI powers Voice AI for platforms that demand global reach, production accuracy, and zero-friction deployment. Our latest improvements represent our continued commitment to delivering on these critical needs. When Calabrio faced growing dissatisfaction with transcription quality, switching to AssemblyAI delivered immediate results: 80% boost in customer satisfaction 22% increase in revenue 63% improvement in developer productivity At Siro , the team heard "wow, that insight was crisp" on 10 out of 10 onboarding calls and saw a 90% reduction in support tickets after switching to Assembly. At Delphi, 50% time savings in clone training freed the team to ship impactful features instead of getting stuck in the weeds. No matter the use case, the quality and experience improvements are felt immediately as soon as customers start building on AssemblyAI. What makes this possible? Industry-leading accuracy We benchmark our models on hundreds of hours of real-world audio, including customer calls, medical dictations, live meetings, and accented speech, to make sure we can confidently say that we lead the industry in accuracy. Build, deploy, and scale Voice AI apps faster than ever AI-native companies are redefining how products are built and shipped, and speed to value has never mattered more. AssemblyAI customers go from first test to production in days, not months. Integrations are described as “plug-and-play” and “frictionless,” with teams reporting 63% less error-handling code after switching. That means faster proofs of concept, quicker launches, and measurable business impact within weeks, not quarters. But speed alone isn’t enough. As Mike Adams from Grain said, “Everything comes down to garbage in, garbage out. The quality of your speech-to-text directly impacts the quality of your analysis.” With our new products, you don’t have to choose between accuracy and agility. title: US Federal Government Customer Experience Suffers Its First-Ever Significant Decline
summary: Forrester’s 2026 US Customer Experience Index (CX Index™) rankings reveal the federal government’s first significant CX decline since 2016, as seven agencies saw scores fall and none improved.
body_text: Each year, Forrester publishes its US Customer Experience Index (CX Index™) rankings, benchmarking CX quality across 11 industries plus the US federal government. This ranking is based on an annual survey given to 95,573 respondents. While the US federal government has historically ranked near the bottom of the industries we study, 2026 delivered a triple whammy: The average US federal CX Index score dropped a statistically significant 2.5 points on our 100-point scale — from 61.9 in 2025 to 59.4 in 2026. That is the lowest US federal average since 2018. This is the US government’s first significant year-over-year decline since we began measuring federal CX in 2016. The US federal government was one of only three verticals that declined in 2026, along with airlines and credit card issuers. In contrast, six private sector industries improved and the overall private sector average improved for the first time in four years, widening the gap between the experiences customers have with federal agencies and the private sector. Forrester’s CX Index Results For US Federal Government Agencies, 2026 In 2026, seven agencies had statistically significant declines and none improved. This marks a sharp reversal from 2025, when four agencies improved and none declined. These findings suggest that sustaining CX improvements is becoming more challenging across the federal government. The National Park Service (NPS) maintained its position as the highest-scoring US federal agency for the 10th consecutive year, earning a score of 74.0. What’s more, it stood alone as the leader, 9.7 points ahead of the Bureau of Consular Affairs — the largest gap between the top two organizations in any industry we studied this year. In contrast, perennial low performers USAJOBS.gov and HealthCare.gov trailed again, with similar scores of 48.9 and 48.4, respectively. The 25.6-point gap between the highest- and lowest-scoring federal organizations is the widest of any vertical we studied. The Biggest Improvement Opportunities Are The Basics Understanding which factors most influence CX helps agencies prioritize investments. That’s why our annual study identifies key CX drivers for every vertical. For the US federal government, this year’s most influential drivers highlight the importance of both frontline service and digital capability. The four most important CX drivers across the US federal government are: Employees at the agency office answer all of my questions Has high-quality information, products, services, or benefits Resolves problems/issues quickly Has a website that meets my needs Want To Learn More? Read The Full Report. Federal CX leaders can influence customer perception of all these drivers. And Forrester can help! For more analysis and information about the drivers and emotions that have the strongest effect on CX, read Forrester’s US Federal Government Customer Experience Index Rankings, 2026 . Share

title: Ryde Signs Memorandum of Understanding with VinaTaxi to Explore Strategic Mobility Expansion in Vietnam
body_text: SINGAPORE, SG / ACCESS Newswire / April 29, 2026 / Ryde Group Ltd (NYSE: RYDE ) ("Ryde" or the "Company"), a leading technology platform for mobility and quick commerce in Singapore, today announced its it has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (" MOU ") with VinaTaxi, a licensed taxi operator in Vietnam, to explore potential strategic collaboration opportunities in Vietnam's fast-growing mobility and electric transport market. This milestone marks an important step in Ryde's regional expansion strategy and supports its continued efforts to evaluate scalable growth opportunities across Southeast Asia's emerging mobility ecosystems. Exploring Entry into Vietnam's High-Growth Mobility Market Under the MOU, Ryde and VinaTaxi will explore a potential collaboration framework to modernise and enhance mobility services in Vietnam. The discussions will focus on leveraging Ryde's proprietary ride-hailing technology and VinaTaxi's established operational fleet to assess opportunities across both four-wheel and two-wheel mobility segments. The areas of exploration include the potential deployment of Ryde's platform within VinaTaxi's existing taxi fleet, the development of an electric motorcycle ride-hailing ecosystem tailored to Vietnam's unique urban transport landscape, and the phased introduction of electric vehicles to support long-term sustainability objectives. Vietnam: A High-Potential and Structurally Attractive Mobility Market Vietnam represents one of Southeast Asia's most dynamic mobility markets, characterised by rapid urbanisation, strong reliance on motorcycle-based transportation, and increasing demand for digital mobility solutions. The government's ongoing focus on electrification and sustainable transport further reinforces the long-term potential of the sector. Through this collaboration, Ryde aims to assess the viability of its platform in a high-volume, fast-growing market while gaining early insight into consumer behaviour, regulatory dynamics, and operational scalability in Vietnam. Strategic Optionality Through Asset-Light Exploration The MOU supports Ryde's broader strategy of combining platform technology with selective market exploration to identify scalable growth opportunities across Asia. By working with an established local operator such as VinaTaxi, Ryde is able to evaluate market entry pathways in a capital-efficient and low-risk manner, while preserving full flexibility for future strategic decisions. "Vietnam represents a highly attractive and fast-evolving mobility market, particularly in the areas of motorcycle and electric mobility," said a spokesperson for Ryde. "This MOU with VinaTaxi allows us to explore potential opportunities in a structured and disciplined manner, leveraging our technology platform while working with a strong local operator. Importantly, this is an exploratory step, and no capital commitment is required at this stage as we assess the market and potential long-term fit." Advancing Ryde's Regional Growth Strategy This collaboration reflects Ryde's ongoing strategy to evaluate and expand into selected high-growth Asian markets through partnerships that combine technology, local operational expertise, and scalable mobility infrastructure. By engaging with established operators in key regional markets, Ryde aims to strengthen its platform network, enhance technology deployment opportunities, and build long-term optionality for sustainable regional growth. title: How to Turn Emails Into Calendar Events Automatically With AI
summary: Learn how to turn emails into calendar events automatically. Skip manual data entry and brittle Zapier flows with AI-native tools built for high-volume…
body_text: It's 4:15 PM on a Friday. A potential lead asks for a 20-minute intro next Tuesday morning. You're between meetings, on your phone. You open the email, check your calendar app, remember the available slots, toggle back to the email, type them out, and wait. Once they reply, you go back into the calendar and manually create the event. This loop runs ten times a day for a busy founder. Most people accept this friction as the cost of doing business. They treat their inbox and their calendar as two separate islands, and that gap is where high-stakes meetings fall through the cracks. In a high-growth environment, the manual labor required to turn emails into calendar events consumes a significant portion of an operator's week. Traditional hacks like forwarding to a special address or using basic keyword triggers don't solve the problem. They just move the friction to a different screen. Real automation requires a system that understands human intent at the inbox layer. Why Manual Email-to-Calendar Entry Is a Bigger Time Sink Than It Looks Manual data entry is not just a nuisance. It's a cognitive tax that breaks deep work cycles. Every time you leave your inbox to create a calendar event, you context switch. Interruptions to deep work often cause significant delays in regaining full focus. If you schedule five meetings a day, you effectively spend your entire afternoon in a state of partial attention. The hidden cost is transcription errors. You read 10:00 AM PST but your calendar is set to EST. You copy the Zoom link but miss the passcode in the previous thread. These small mistakes lead to the dreaded empty meeting room. For chiefs of staff and executive assistants, the burden is heavier. They manage multiple schedules where a single typo in a calendar invite can derail a partnership. Founders often try to solve this by hiring an EA too early or by using complex booking links. Booking links help, but they're often perceived as cold or impersonal in high-touch sales and investor relations. The recipient has to do the work for you. A better approach keeps the interaction in the email thread while the heavy lifting happens in the background. If your current workflow involves more than two clicks to go from a confirmed time to a calendar invite, the system is broken. You are performing a task that a transformer model can execute in milliseconds with 100% accuracy. The goal is to move from manual transcription to intent-based confirmation. How Gmail's Native Event Detection Works (And Where It Falls Short) Google Workspace provides a basic level of event detection. Google Workspace includes features designed to highlight and identify potential scheduling details within a message. This system relies on pattern matching. It looks for specific strings like "Monday at 4 PM" or "October 12th." If the email structure is standard, like an airline reservation or a concert ticket, Gmail creates a Google Calendar event automatically. This pattern matching fails the moment a conversation gets ambiguous. If a contact writes "Let's aim for sometime late Tuesday or perhaps Wednesday before lunch," the native Gmail parser usually ignores it. It also struggles with time zones. If the sender is in London and you are in San Francisco, the native tool often defaults to your local time without verifying the sender's intent. This results in meetings scheduled for 3:00 AM. The Gmail sidebar still requires you to manually verify every detail. You click the date, check the time, add the title, invite the guests. It's a digital stencil, not an automated assistant. For a founder-led sales process, this is insufficient. You need a tool that understands the context of the entire thread. Gmail treats every email as an isolated document. It does not remember that you told this specific person you are unavailable on Fridays. To truly turn emails into calendar events, the software must have a memory of your previous interactions and your specific preferences. Relying on Google's default tools means you are still the primary coordinator. The Add-On Approach: Mail2Cal, Fwd2Cal, and Chrome Extensions The first wave of solutions involved Chrome extensions and forwarding services. Forwarding services allow users to send an email to a designated address to generate a calendar draft. Other extensions add a "Create Event" button directly into the Gmail interface. These tools solve the basic transcription problem but introduce new security and workflow hurdles. Every Chrome extension you install is a potential privacy risk. Many of these tools require broad permissions to read and change your data on all websites. For VCs and founders handling sensitive deal flow, this is often a dealbreaker. Security-conscious teams now look for SOC 2 Type II certified platforms instead of unverified browser add-ons. Workflow friction remains the biggest issue. You still have to trigger the action manually. You highlight the text, click the extension icon, then fix the errors the extension made. It's a wrapper around the existing problem. These tools also fail to sync across devices. If you are on the mobile Gmail app, your desktop Chrome extension is useless. You're back to manual entry the moment you leave your desk. High-volume inboxes require server-side intelligence that works everywhere. If an automation only works when you're at your laptop with a specific browser open, it's a band-aid. True efficiency comes from a unified system that recognizes a scheduling intent regardless of the device you use. You should be able to triage your inbox and book meetings with the same ease on a phone as you do on a desktop. Why Zapier and Automation Platforms Add Complexity Without Solving the Root Problem Zapier and Make are the standard answers for connecting Gmail to Google Calendar. A typical workflow involves a trigger (New Starred Email) and an action (Create Detailed Event). On paper, this looks like the perfect way to turn emails into calendar events. In practice, these workflows are brittle and require constant maintenance. The core problem is that Zapier is a logic engine, not an intelligence engine. It works well for structured data. If every email you received followed a strict template, Zapier would be flawless. But human communication is messy. If someone replies "Actually, can we push that to 3?" the Zapier flow will either fail or create a duplicate event. It cannot follow the thread of a conversation. You also end up managing two separate systems. When the automation fails, you dig into the Zapier task history to find out why. You become a part-time automation engineer instead of a founder. The complexity of setting up multi-step Zaps for different scenarios (rescheduling vs. new meetings) creates a new kind of busywork. These platforms also lack the context of your current calendar. They can create an event, but they cannot tell you if that event conflicts with a high-priority board meeting unless you build an even more complex web of logic. Most operators find that after a few weeks of troubleshooting, they go back to manual entry because it feels more reliable. Automation should reduce your mental load, not give you a new dashboard to monitor. What AI-Native Email Clients Do Differently: Intent Detection at the Inbox Layer AI-native email clients like Slashy represent a real shift in how software handles scheduling. Instead of waiting for a manual trigger, the AI operates at the inbox layer. It reads incoming mail and identifies the underlying intent. If a recruiter asks for an interview, the system recognizes this as a scheduling request before you even open the thread. This is not simple keyword matching. It is semantic understanding. Slashy uses a proprietary memory system. It learns your writing voice and your specific scheduling preferences over time. It knows that you prefer morning meetings for deep work and afternoon slots for intro calls. Because it has access to both your email and your calendar in one interface, it can draft a reply with your actual availability included. This eliminates the back-and-forth entirely. You can book calls without the back-and-forth by letting the AI handle the proposal and the confirmation. The intelligence extends to the calendar sidebar. When you are looking at an email, the sidebar does not just show your schedule. It allows you to check your availability and manage your schedule directly alongside your emails. This turns the calendar from a grid of boxes into a command center. Because Slashy is built on top of Gmail, you get the reliability of Google's infrastructure with an intelligence layer that actually does the work. It's the difference between a tool that waits for instructions and an assistant that anticipates your needs. This is why AI-first clients for founders are replacing traditional apps. They handle the administrative overhead so you can focus on the content of the meeting. How to Set Up Automatic Email-to-Calendar Conversion in Slashy Setting up automatic scheduling in Slashy takes three minutes. There are no complex Zapier webhooks or browser extensions to configure. Because Slashy is a native client, it connects directly to your Gmail and Google Calendar accounts with a single secure login. The platform ensures that user information is protected through industry-standard security protocols. First, you connect your accounts. Slashy supports a unified inbox view, so you can manage multiple professional and personal calendars in one place. Once connected, you define your scheduling preferences. You tell the AI which blocks are for internal work and which are open for external guests. The system then begins monitoring your threads for scheduling intent. When an email arrives that requires a meeting, Slashy drafts a reply in your voice. It includes your availability directly based on your live schedule. To turn an email into a calendar event, you click the 'Add to calendar' prompt or use the Google Calendar icon in the side panel. If you are on the go, you can use the iMessage interface to tell Slashy to book a meeting. You text the AI, and it updates your calendar. The system also handles follow-ups. If a recipient hasn't picked a time, Slashy can send a follow-up ping automatically so important deals never go cold. A deal never goes cold because of a scheduling bottleneck. What to Expect: Fewer Missed Meetings, Less Context Switching When you move from manual entry to an AI-native workflow, the first thing you notice is the silence. The constant ping-pong of "Does this time work?" disappears. You gain back hours of productive time. More importantly, you eliminate the anxiety of the missed invite. You no longer have to double-check whether you actually sent that calendar link or whether the guest accepted it. The system tracks it for you. The integration with other tools adds another layer of efficiency. If you use a CRM, you can sync Gmail conversations to Attio alongside your calendar events. This creates a full audit trail of every interaction with a prospect. You can see when they opened the email, what device they used, and exactly when the meeting was booked. This visibility matters for sales teams and recruiters who need to move fast. Context switching becomes a thing of the past. Instead of jumping between three different tabs to schedule a single call, you stay in one flow. The calendar sidebar provides the prep you need right before the meeting starts. It's a more professional experience for your recipients too. They receive a clean, accurate invite immediately after the time is agreed upon. They see a founder who is organized and responsive. By automating the transition from email to calendar, you save time and improve the quality of your professional relationships. You're free to focus on the conversation rather than the coordinates. Conclusion Turning emails into calendar events should not be a manual task in 2026. The technology exists to interpret human intent and manage schedules without your involvement. Manual entry and brittle automation are relics of an era where software was a passive tool. Your inbox should be an active participant in your productivity. Slashy is built specifically for founders and operators who cannot afford to waste five hours a week on administrative overhead. It handles the drafting, the availability sharing, and the event creation so you can stay focused on actual work. Stop acting as your own secretary and start using an inbox that thinks. Sign up for Slashy and experience the first email client that understands exactly what your next meeting should be.

title: 57% of US adults recommended a statin under new guidelines
summary: The science behind why the guidelines moved treatment earlier.
body_text: 57% of US adults recommended a statin under new guidelines Brandon Ballinger · Jul 24, 2026 A cardiologist I worked with once joked that statins are so effective that we should just put them in the water supply. He might be getting his wish. The 2026 cholesterol guidelines recommend earlier treatment, and a new study out today estimates that 57% of US adults would be recommended a statin under the new guidelines. I’m a bit split. On the one hand, it can feel like obvious over-medicalization to put half of society on a prescription drug. On the other hand, biomedical science has advanced to the point where it’s conceivable to eradicate heart disease: we can predict risk 30 years in advance, have biomedicines that cut cholesterol by 80% or more , including an oral PCSK9 inhibitor approved just last week, and novel biomarkers let us refine risk prediction beyond traditional LDL cholesterol. At some level, it becomes silly to let a preventable health condition make an abattoir of society when we have the biomedical tools to solve it. For the rest of this article, I’ll review some of the science underlying why medical societies are recommending heart disease treatment start earlier than before. We’ll start with mechanisms, then go into statistical models and biomarkers, new drugs (including statin alternatives), and wrap up with some society-wide implications. Cholesterol exposure works like cigarette pack-years If you smoke a pack of cigarettes, you don’t get lung cancer that same afternoon. Risk comes from dose times years, which is why oncologists count cigarette exposure in terms of pack-years. We’ve increasingly learned that cholesterol behaves the same way. ApoB-containing particles (LDL, VLDL remnants, and Lp(a)) cross the artery wall, deposit cholesterol, and the deposits grow over the course of decades. As a result, what predicts a heart attack is the area under your LDL curve. Cardiologists have started formally calling this measure “cholesterol-years” . For example, a personw ith an average LDL of 125 mg/dL for 40 years has accumulated 5,000 mg/dL-years. The estimate is that roughly 5,000 mg/dL-years is the threshold at which enough plaque has accumulated for events to start happening. At an LDL of 100 mg/dL, you’d cross that line around age 50. At 160 mg/dL, you’d cross it around age 31. We know this theory is true in part due to autopsies of people aged 15-34 who died of accidents, homicides, and suicides. Those autopsies show raised fatty streaks in the right coronary arteries for about 10% of 15-to-19-year-olds and about 30% of 30-to-34-year-olds. Cross-sections are schematic. Lesion prevalence from PDAY . Serial CT angiography finds the same pattern in living people. NATURE-CT scanned 205 adults with low calcium scores. Over 5 years, plaque volume roughly doubled. Soft plaque doubled over five years in a non-symptomatic population. Source: Aldana-Bitar et al., NATURE-CT, 2026 . Beyond LDL cholesterol, independent risk factors like Lp(a) , blood pressure, and inflammation act as multipliers on the base risk. Statistical models now predict risk 30 years out The old cardiovascular Pooled Cohort Equations answered one question: what’s your chance of a heart attack in the next 10 years? For a healthy 35-year-old, the answer is always “low,” which is why young people were almost never recommended a statin. The new PREVENT equations predict both 10-year and 30-year risk. They cover ages 30 to 79 instead of 40 to 75, incorporate kidney function, drop race as an input, and optionally factor in social factors via zip code. The 30-year estimate drives nearly all of the new statin recommendations. You can see why on the risk curve itself. If you take one person with modestly high cholesterol (non-HDL-C 160, HDL 45), normal blood pressure, no diabetes, and no smoking, and run PREVENT at each age, their 10-year risk stays under 5% until their sixties but their 30-year risk crosses 10% (the level at which medication starts to become recommended) at about age 45. The same person is far below the treatment line on 10-year risk and above it on 30-year risk for most of midlife. Computed from the AHA PREVENT equations . The JAMA study referenced above found 57% of US adults would be recommended a statin for primary prevention, up from 42.7% under the 2018 guidelines, which is 21.5 million more people. A companion NHANES analysis (a preprint from a different group) shows the bulk of the expansion comes in middle aged people: The 30-year criterion applies only to ages 30–59, and that’s where the added recommendations concentrate. Source: Diao et al., preprint, 2026 , class 2 threshold. Absolute eligibility still climbs with age (about 11% of people in their 30s are recommended a statin, versus 85% in their 60s and 93% in their 70s), but almost everyone in their 70s already qualified under the old rules too. The genuinely new group is middle-aged. The newly eligible are younger and lower-risk than the people who already qualified: mean 10-year risk of 3.1% versus 6.1%. This is the design working as intended, and it’s also the fair objection. A 3.1% ten-year risk means about 97 out of 100 people won’t have an event in the next decade whether or not they take anything, and the case for treating them rests on a 30-year projection that hasn’t directly been tested in clinical trials. (Medication trials run five years. The genetic evidence is the substitute, and it’s good evidence, but it’s inference rather than a randomized answer.) New biomarkers refine risk estimates A 30-year projection built on a standard lipid panel is a 30-year projection built on one of the three biological pathways that cause atherosclerosis. Better inputs are cheap and available now. ApoB counts atherogenic particles instead of estimating the cholesterol inside them. In about 20% of people LDL-C reads normal while ApoB is elevated. The 2026 guideline notes that when you assess lipid markers together, “only apoB remains significant” as a predictor of heart attacks. Lp(a) is inherited, stable for life, and untouched by diet or statins. In the HELIUS cohort , the top fifth of Lp(a) carried 1.86× the risk of the bottom fifth, a steeper gradient than LDL-C. About 20% of people have elevated levels, and one test settles it forever. hs-CRP tracks the inflammatory arm. The top fifth carried 1.51× the risk in the same cohort, independent of cholesterol. eGFR and HbA1c pull in kidney and metabolic health. PREVENT already uses eGFR, which is part of why it outperforms the equations it replaced. Since these risk factors are independent, their effects stack rather than overlap. Someone in the top quintile for all three of LDL-C, Lp(a), and hs-CRP had 2.4x the risk of someone elevated on none. One interesting input is blood pressure. It’s still in PREVENT as a single number, but when we analyzed 650,000 connected cuff readings, we found day-to-day systolic swings of 10 mmHg on average, with 20 mmHg swings about 5% of the time. Conceivably, the continuous blood pressure measurements we’re seeing on wearables in 2026 might refine this further. Vitamin D is an open question. Vitamin D is consistently associated with cardiovascular risk in observational data. A 2025 trial in people who’d already had a heart attack found that titrating vitamin Ddoses to a target blood level halved repeat cardiovascular events, which is promising, though very preliminary. If that result holds up, vitamin D may earn a place in future risk models. New drugs are unreasonably effective The arsenal of cardiovascular drugs has never been stronger. Beyond statins, we have ezetimibe and PCSK9 inhibitors (including an oral PCSK9 inhibitor approved last week): Bempedoic acid is the option for the roughly 10% of patients with statin-attributed muscle symptoms. Lipfendra , approved July 16, 2026, is the first PCSK9 inhibitor you can take as a pill. Triple therapy (all three) cuts LDL by 80–85%, into the 20s and 30s mg/dL. At that point, you’re not slowing the accumulation of cholesterol-years, you’re essentially stopping the clock entirely. Care delivery is still a bottleneck All of this biomedical innovation counts for little if the “last mile,” care delivery, fails. And unfortunately, 46% of US counties have zero cardiologists, <1% of patients get the optimal medical therapy described above, and the doctor shortage is getting worse . Someone has to order the ApoB and Lp(a), interpret a 30-year risk estimate, have a real conversation about a decades-long medication, and then actually follow up on the labs six months later. There aren’t enough cardiologists to do that, and there won’t be in our lifetimes. This is an interesting role for AI. Cardiovascular prevention is algready “algorithmic”, driven by protocols. Could cardiovascular prevention scale more like software than clinical visits? Obviously we think so here, and Empirical Health is a bet in this direction. Know your 30-year risk, not just your cholesterol. Empirical Health's heart health panel measures ApoB, Lp(a), hs-CRP, and standard lipids, and runs your numbers through the PREVENT equations. Get your free 30-day heart health guide Evidence-based steps to optimize your heart health.

title: Payment Orchestration – Why it’s Important for Indian Businesses
summary: Explore the importance of payment orchestration for Indian businesses. Understand how it simplifies transactions, boosts success rates, and drives revenue growth with Cashfree Payments' flowWise solution.
body_text: Table of Contents Toggle As Indian businesses strive to meet the increasing expectations of consumers for hassle-free payment processes, they are constantly incorporating new payment methods and expanding their range of payment choices. This shift indicates that the future of payments in India will involve using multiple payment gateways (PGs). However, integrating with multiple PGs requires significant costs and technological effort. Consequently, many businesses in India face challenges in providing the seamless payment experience that modern customers expect. To address this issue, a payment orchestrator becomes essential. What is Payment Orchestration? Payment orchestration is a simple solution that allows businesses to integrate multiple payment gateways and processors with a single API integration and creates a central hub optimising transaction routing, reducing costs, and maximizing payment success rates. Payment orchestration involves integrating and managing the entire payment process, including transaction routing, and settlement. Payment management solutions like flowWise achieves this by connecting businesses with various payment aggregators, acquirers, and banks through a unified software layer. Additionally flowWise also enables your finance team to track critical metrics such as risk, refunds, reconciliation, settlements for all aggregators through a unified dashboard. How does Payment Orchestration/Routing work? Payment Orchestrators can be assumed to be helpful guides that give direction to your payments. They use clever routing mechanisms to figure out the best route for payments. These guides operate through Payment Orchestration Platforms (POPs), directing payments to the most reliable service providers. This reduces problems and makes sure more payments succeed. In a real-life scenario, when a user buys something online and adds it to cart, the payment journey begins. As they go to the checkout page and pick a payment method, the Payment Orchestration Platform takes charge. It manages the whole process, guiding the payment details to a payment gateway . The platform then cleverly sends the payment request to different processors, strategically avoiding issues and increasing the chances of success. By using multiple processors and a smart routing system, payment orchestration avoids payment troubles and boosts success rates. This not only enhances customer experience but also ensures a higher rate of payment success . So, payment orchestration isn’t just about accepting payments – it’s like having a plan that makes every part of the payment journey work better. Benefits of Payment Orchestration to a Business Payment Orchestration Platforms optimize every transaction for increased revenue. These platforms simplify end-to-end payments, leading to enhanced customer experiences, higher online sales, and increased revenue. Let’s deep dive. Seamless Integration with PAs: Through payment orchestration, merchants gain the ability to integrate numerous local and global payment aggregators via a single integration, significantly reducing the time and tech effort required for individual integration. For instance, businesses seeking to offer alternative payment modes can effortlessly connect with a provider that caters to specific customer payment preferences. Diversity in Payment Methods: A key advantage of payment orchestration platforms lies in merchants having access to an extensive array of payment aggregators and modes. As business requirements evolve, these platforms facilitate the seamless addition of multiple payment methods. This proves especially beneficial for companies dealing with a diverse customer base possessing varied payment preferences, encompassing credit or debit cards, mobile wallets, or “ Buy Now, Pay Later ” options. High Success Rate with Intelligent Payment Routing: With orchestration platforms enabling AI/ML-powered as well as rule-based routing, businesses can set up their routing logic to ensure the highest possible success rate and also the flexibility to switch between PGs in cases of payment failures and downtime. High Conversion Rate through Enhanced Customer Experiences: Recognizing that customers are prone to abandoning their shopping carts if the checkout process is overly complex or time-consuming, payment orchestration platforms step in to prevent such occurrences. They achieve this by crafting a streamlined checkout experience that include diverse payment options, saved cards, and intelligent retries across payment gateways. These features collectively contribute to making transactions frictionless for consumers and increasing conversion rates. Reduced Operational Cost through Comprehensive Business Intelligence: A modern orchestration platform goes beyond transaction facilitation. Providing a unified view of PG or mode-level performance, these platforms present insights that enable informed decision-making. Platforms like flowWise offer a unified view of critical metrics such as risk, refunds, reconciliation, settlements for all aggregators through a unified dashboard. Enhanced Revenue Generation: With a simplified payment process, enhanced conversion rate a high payment success rate and reduced operational cost, orchestration platforms set businesses up for driving revenue and strengthen the foundation for business’ sustained growth. Payment Orchestration with Cashfree Payments Cashfree Payments’ flowWise is a one-stop payment management solution that helps businesses not only route payment to achieve up to a 10% higher success rates, and boost their revenue by up to 20%, but also prevent and block fraudulent transactions with its built-in integration with RiskShield . Additionally, flowWise Native, India’s first self-hosted solution gives merchants the flexibility to go-live with payment modes and scale their payments natively in their own environment, leading to data security and 10x lower cost of orchestration. body_text: Fuel represents one of the highest variable costs for businesses that operate vehicles, and selecting the best business credit card for fuel cash back can return meaningful savings on every fill-up. This guide ranks the top business credit cards for fuel cash back and explains when a dedicated fuel card delivers greater value than percentage-based rewards programs. You will learn how fuel cash back works, what criteria matter most when evaluating cards, and which options suit small business owners with different fleet sizes and spending patterns. Why Fuel Cash Back Cards Save Your Fleet Money Business credit cards that offer cash back on fuel purchases return a percentage of every dollar spent at qualifying locations. For operators wondering if fuel cards save you money , this rewards structure works well for small businesses with predictable fuel expenses because every fill-up generates automatic savings credited to the account. However, not all cards are structured the same way. Some cards offer: Flat cash back on gas purchases Bonus rewards on gas within specific merchant categories Rotating fuel rewards categories Statement credit offers after spending thresholds are met Other cards focus on travel or dining rather than fleet operations. For fleets with larger fuel volume, fleet cards typically provide stronger long-term savings because they reduce fuel prices directly through per-gallon discounts instead of relying only on cash back rewards. Understanding spending caps Many business rewards cards place spending caps on bonus fuel categories before standard rewards rates apply. For example, some programs limit elevated rewards to the first $25,000 to $50,000 in eligible annual purchases before lower base rates apply. See issuer terms for current limits and reward structures.1 Cash back vs. per-gallon discounts Cash back differs fundamentally from per-gallon discounts offered by fleet fuel cards . With cash back, you earn a percentage of the total transaction amount. Per-gallon discounts reduce the price before payment, which typically delivers greater savings for high-volume fuel buyers. Understanding this distinction helps fleet operators choose the best card for cash back on fuel based on their spending patterns. How to Evaluate Business Credit Cards for Fuel Cash Back Selecting the right business gas credit card requires examining several factors beyond the headline rewards rate, rather than simply comparing headline percentages. Consider these evaluation criteria: Fuel rewards rate - Higher percentages maximize returns on every transaction Spending caps - Annual limits determine when bonus rates expire Annual fee - Calculate whether projected annual savings exceed card costs Station acceptance - Confirm the card works at the truck stops your drivers actually use Employee cards - Verify that additional cards carry no extra fees Credit score requirements - Most cards require good to excellent credit to qualify, making building business credit essential for approval Fraud controls - Assess available spending limits and transaction alerts But also, many business gas card products include: Free employee and virtual cards Expense tracking tools Online account management Mobile apps to track fuel spend in real time Understanding these differences helps fleets choose the best business card for operational efficiency rather than just short-term rewards. Important merchant category restrictions Some fuel card types exclude purchases at warehouse clubs, supercenters, or truck stops from the bonus fuel category. Always verify merchant category definitions before applying. When to consider fleet-specific alternatives Businesses with growing fuel volume should also evaluate fleet fuel cards that offer per-gallon discounts and driver-level spend controls beyond what traditional business credit cards provide. For operations requiring prepaid options, explore the best prepaid fuel cards available today. 10 Best Business Credit Cards for Fuel Cash Back The following business credit cards and fleet payment platforms were evaluated based on fuel savings, operational controls, reporting capabilities, fees, and suitability for businesses with regular fuel spend. 1. This platform may be a stronger fit for growing fleets that require more than percentage-based cash back rewards alone. 2. WEX Fleet Card WEX provides fleet fuel cards with reporting, spend controls, and fuel management tools through the WEX Nationwide Savings Network. The platform is commonly used by commercial fleets seeking transaction visibility and fuel purchase tracking across multiple drivers and vehicles. Fleets evaluating WEX may also compare integrated financial platforms that combine fuel payments with payroll, expense management, and operational reporting tools. 3. Fuelman Fuelman offers fuel management tools, reporting, and rebate programs through participating fuel networks. The platform focuses primarily on fuel purchasing controls and transaction management for commercial fleets. Costs and savings may vary depending on network usage, billing structure, and monthly fuel volume. 4. Mudflap Mudflap focuses on fuel discount programs for owner-operators and smaller fleets through participating truck stop networks and app-based fueling tools. The platform is designed primarily around fuel savings, while fleets requiring broader spend controls, accounting visibility, and integrated financial tools may require more comprehensive fleet management platforms. 5. Ink Business Cash® Credit Card The Ink Business Cash® Credit Card is one of the best gas cash back card options for smaller fleets with moderate fuel expenses and lower monthly fleet spend. Key features include: Fuel and dining cash back categories No annual fee Cash back rewards on select business purchases beyond fuel This business credit card may work well for smaller operations seeking simple cash back on gas purchases without fleet-specific management tools. 6. U.S. Bank Triple Cash Rewards Visa® Business Card This Visa® business card focuses on cash back on eligible purchases at gas and EV charging stations. How to Pick the Right Fuel Cash Back Card Selecting the best credit cards for fuel depends on fleet size, monthly fuel volume, and whether your operation needs controls beyond standard rewards. title: How to Master SMS Marketing: Key Takeaways from My Talk on the Advisory Board Podcast
summary: Boostly CEO Ryan Roberts shares key SMS marketing strategies from The Advisory Board Podcast—covering compliance, timing, and creative engagement.
body_text: How to Master SMS Marketing: Key Takeaways from My Talk on the Advisory Board Podcast I recently had the opportunity to join Dave Hansen on The Advisory Board Podcast to discuss one of my favorite topics: SMS marketing. As the CEO of Boostly, I’m passionate about helping businesses in the restaurant and franchise industries connect with their customers in more meaningful ways using SMS. In our conversation, Dave and I explored a range of topics, from compliance and strategy to the innovative ways brands can use SMS to engage with their audience. If you missed the episode, don’t worry! I’ll break down some of the key points we covered. You can also listen to the full episode on YouTube or find it on Spreaker . The Importance of Opt-In Consent and Compliance One of the key messages I shared during the episode is that compliance in SMS marketing isn’t just a box to check—it’s essential. The Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) requires businesses to gather explicit opt-in consent before sending marketing texts. I stressed that failing to comply can lead to significant fines, up to $500 per message per person. To help avoid these pitfalls, it’s crucial to choose vendors that enforce automated opt-in and opt-out processes, protecting your brand and your bottom line. As I mentioned in the episode, “The most fundamental component is gathering opt-in consent. You can’t just start texting people just because you have their phone number.” Getting this part right not only keeps your brand compliant but also builds a foundation of trust with your audience. Beyond Discounts: Creative Engagement A large part of our conversation focused on going beyond the typical SMS promotions. While discounts are a staple, over-reliance on them can devalue your brand in the long term. Instead, I recommended exploring creative strategies like gamification and branded content. For example, some of our clients have successfully used “lottery texts,” where customers can reply with a number for a chance to win a reward. These kinds of campaigns can boost engagement rates from a standard 3-5% to as high as 40-50%. One restaurant owner even sends weekly dad jokes to his customers, building a lighthearted connection that keeps his brand top of mind. It’s these small, creative touches that help businesses stand out in a crowded market. Timing is Everything We also covered the power of timing when it comes to SMS marketing. Sending the right message at the right moment can make all the difference. For instance, in the food industry, it’s smart to send dinner promotions around 4:00 PM when customers are beginning to think about their evening plans. I shared that aligning your messaging with the customer’s decision-making point is crucial for increasing response rates. “If you’re just looking to maximize the amount of revenue, you want to do it right before they would normally be evaluating alternatives,” I explained during the podcast. By understanding your audience’s behavior, you can optimize your SMS strategy for the best results. Adding Value to Build Trust Another strategy we discussed was using SMS not just as a sales channel but as a way to build trust and offer value to your customers. This can include sharing expert advice, helpful tips, or even reminders about events and special programs. The goal is to position your brand as a trusted resource and not just a place to transact. By applying these strategies, businesses can elevate their SMS marketing efforts and build deeper, more meaningful relationships with their audience. To listen to the entire podcast episode, visit YouTube or catch it on Spreaker . If you have questions or want to explore how Boostly can help your business, feel free to reach out. Happy texting!

body_text: Parsons Accelerates Industrial Base Modernization and Advanced Manufacturing to Deliver Mission Readiness at Speed and Scale 07/21/2026 PDF Version Key Takeaways: Parsons delivers integrated industrial base modernization and advanced manufacturing solutions that accelerate mission readiness across defense and infrastructure markets worldwide. Parsons’ enterprise-wide delivery model unites expertise across its Federal Solutions and Critical Infrastructure segments to deliver complete industrial ecosystems at speed and scale. With global execution and proven programs, Parsons supports urgent national security and economic priorities driven by rising demand and sustained government investment in industrial capacity. CHANTILLY, Va., July 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Parsons Corporation (NYSE: PSN) today highlighted its delivery of integrated industrial base modernization and advanced manufacturing solutions that are strengthening national security, enabling global infrastructure resilience, and accelerating delivery of mission-critical capabilities across defense and commercial markets. As demand intensifies to modernize aging infrastructure and scale production of critical capabilities, Parsons delivers integrated, end-to-end solutions that transform how industrial capacity is built, modernized, and sustained. By combining deep engineering expertise, advanced technologies, and global program delivery, the company enables customers to expand production, strengthen supply chains, and deliver operational capability in real time. “Industrial base modernization is no longer a future priority; it’s an immediate operational requirement,” said Martin Boson, president of Engineered Systems for Parsons. “We are helping redefine how the defense industrial base is modernized, integrating advanced manufacturing, infrastructure, and digital capabilities to rapidly scale production, improve readiness, and deliver mission-critical capacity for today’s and tomorrow’s threats.” Parsons differentiates through a fully integrated delivery model that unifies planning, engineering, program and construction management, advanced manufacturing, cybersecurity, and environmental solutions expertise into a single approach. This enables the company to deliver complete industrial ecosystems rather than standalone facilities, accelerating timelines, reducing risk, and ensuring mission success. By leveraging capabilities across both its Federal Solutions and Critical Infrastructure segments, Parsons bridges traditionally siloed markets and delivers mission-aligned solutions at scale. “Industrial base modernization requires more than expanding production; it demands the infrastructure, energy, and systems that sustain it,” said Mark Fialkowski, president of Infrastructure North America for Parsons. “We are delivering integrated solutions across critical infrastructure, from data centers and energy systems to industrial development, to help our customers strengthen resilience, enable economic growth, and build the industrial ecosystems needed to support both national security and commercial demands.” Parsons’ capabilities span the full spectrum of defense industrial base modernization priorities, from modernizing Army munitions and ammunition facilities to upgrading legacy infrastructure across depots, arsenals, and manufacturing plants. This is demonstrated by the company’s growing role in the U.S. Army’s Organic Industrial Base, including a $169.5 million design-build contract with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to deliver a new Ammonium Nitrate Solution Tank Farm at Holston Army Ammunition Plant. The company also supports expanded production capacity through work on Nammo’s new rocket motor production facility in Perry, Florida , strengthening production scale, supply chain resilience, and operational readiness. The company also delivers complex energetics and specialized facilities, as demonstrated by the Blue Grass Chemical Weapons Stockpile Destruction Project , where Parsons played a central role in the design, construction, operation, and closure of the facility that safely eliminated the nation’s remaining chemical weapons stockpile in support of critical national security objectives. This legacy chemical demilitarization expertise reflects Parsons’ ability to execute highly complex, high-consequence industrial programs requiring advanced safety, regulatory, environmental, and operational expertise. Beyond the United States, Parsons is executing large-scale industrial and infrastructure programs globally. In the Middle East, the company is advancing economic diversification and industrial growth through initiatives such as the Al Karaana Special Economic Zone in Qatar . Our long record of developing large industrial cities and special economic zones in Saudi Arabia, dating back to the 1970s, such as Jazan and Yanbu Industrial Cities , enables integrated development and long-term resilience. Parsons also delivers mission-critical data center infrastructure across the region to support AI, digital transformation, and secure operations, while strengthening supply chains tied to critical minerals and advanced manufacturing. In parallel, Parsons is advancing high-tech manufacturing ecosystems, including semiconductor-related infrastructure that strengthens domestic and allied production capacity and enables more resilient supply chains through critical minerals sourcing, processing, and distribution. The company further integrates digital engineering, environmental remediation, and critical infrastructure protection to modernize legacy industrial sites and enable next-generation manufacturing. By combining lifecycle optimization, regulatory alignment, and mission-critical cybersecurity and physical protection, the company delivers resilient, high-performance facilities designed for sustained operations in complex and contested environments. Its program advisory expertise, including long-standing support to the Department of Energy and the Department of War, helps translate evolving mission requirements into executable infrastructure investments that strengthen the full industrial ecosystem from production through distribution. Parsons also delivers the critical infrastructure that powers and sustains industrial capacity, including energy and microgrid solutions and industrial water and wastewater systems. In addition, the company is also advancing nuclear energy solutions critical to powering next-generation industrial capacity and strengthening energy resilience. The integrated energy capabilities are delivered across the full lifecycle, supporting both national security missions and commercial energy infrastructure, including energy-intensive industries such as advanced manufacturing and data centers. These capabilities extend across North America, the Middle East, and other key markets, including Canada, where Parsons supports infrastructure and industrial development aligned with national growth and resource priorities. This global reach, combined with deep technical expertise, positions Parsons to deliver consistent, high-impact outcomes across diverse operational environments. Demand for industrial base modernization continues to accelerate, driven by geopolitical competition, supply chain vulnerabilities, and significant government investment in munitions production, advanced manufacturing, and critical infrastructure. Parsons is directly aligned with these priorities, helping customers respond to urgent operational needs while building long-term resilience. With decades of experience delivering complex industrial and infrastructure programs, Parsons continues to enable the next generation of scalable, resilient, and secure industrial capacity, delivering capability at the speed and scale today’s missions demand. To learn more about Parsons’ industrial base modernization capabilities, visit parsons.com/industrial-base-modernization/ and parsons.com/manufacturing/ .
